items.summary: Researchers at the University of Rochester and Technion–Israel Institute of Technology accidentally discovered a new way to rearrange the internal structure of molybdenum—an extremely heat-resistant metal—at room temperature. Molybdenum is typically used to reinforce nuclear reactors, jet engine turbine blades and rocket nozzles because it doesn't melt until it is heated to more than 2,600°C (4,712°F). Controlling its atomic structure at room temperature could open the door to more applications, including next-generation semiconductors.

Lower gasoline prices during October offer some relief on the energy side. -- The monthly numbers should show prices rising more slowly than in September, but the shutdown gap means the annual inflation rate everyone quotes will be an estimate this time. items.summary: Mid-infrared observations with the Subaru Telescope have revealed the shape and surface temperature of the nucleus of Comet 2P/Encke. They also determined that the surface temperature at the time of observation was 328 ± 7 Kelvin (about 55°C).

Not a 'night owl' yet: Extraordinary bird fossil from Messel Pit suggests species still hunted by day
items.summary: An exceptionally well-preserved, approximately 47-million-year-old owl fossil from the UNESCO World Heritage Site Messel provides new clues as to when owls became nocturnal. The newly described species Masillastrix blattophaga was likely still diurnal—as indicated by an iridescent cockroach in its stomach, as well as the structure of its feathers and wing bones. In their new study, published in the journal Current Biology, the Senckenberg researchers speculate that nocturnal behavior in owls only developed between the middle and late Eocene, some 47 to 34 million years ago.

Jameis Winston came in to replace J.J. McCarthy early in the second half on Sunday afternoon in Philadelphia. McCarthy, on just their second play of the third quarter, scrambled for a few yards up the left side. But as he went down, McCarthy turned and lowered his right shoulder — which was then drilled hard by Eagles linebacker Zack Baun. McCarthy was quickly replaced by backup Jameis Winston, and went over to the sidelines. Clearly, though, McCarthy's shoulder was a big problem. He was seen trying to throw the ball on the sidelines, but he was in so much pain and actually dropped down to the ground after screaming out. He slammed his helmet down to the bench out of frustration, too.

On 3rd-and-8 with 1:45 to play, Colts coach Shane Steichen called a pass instead of running clock before a field goal attempt. Why that was the right call Facing a third-and-8 at the Dallas 32-yard line with 1:45 left in Sunday's game, Steichen called a pass play in order to try to get the first down instead of handing it off in an effort to run clock. The Cowboys had just used their final timeout, Indianapolis had one down left at its disposal and Steichen knew Dallas would have enough time to drive into range for a game-tying field goal even if he ran off an extra 40 seconds in that situation.

If you've ever noticed plumes of heavy smoke emanating from an F1 car it might be something cold rather than something hot — here's how F1 teams use dry ice. Dry ice is carbon dioxide in solid form, sitting at a bone-chilling -109.3 degrees Fahrenheit. It doesn't melt into liquid like ice water — instead, it sublimates directly into gas, which makes it perfect for cooling high-performance components without leaving behind any moisture. That's key when you're dealing with tightly packaged electronics, batteries, and driver cockpits that are not water-friendly.

James Madison tied a Kentucky opponent record by attempting 45 3-pointers on Friday. The sheer volume of perimeter shots tied a program record for a Kentucky opponent, proving that heavy underdogs will use the 3-point line as the ultimate equalizer against Mark Pope's squad. Facing a significant talent and height disparity, the Dukes opted to space the floor and let it fly. It is a classic survival strategy for undersized teams. Hit enough outside shots, and you neutralize the paint advantage. James Madison executed that plan relentlessly, connecting on 15 of those attempts to keep the game uncomfortably close for most of the night.

Med spas are raving about vitamin B12 shots as a pick-me-up. But do they actually make you feel more energized? I f you spend time on social media, you may have seen med spa owners and employees describing vitamin B12 shots as a pick-me-up . When they’re run down or facing a busy week, they say, a quick injection gets them through. Some med spas say many people feel an energy lift within a day or two and recommend a shot every few weeks. New figures suggest hazel dormice may be recovering after decades of decline, with warmer summers boosting survival. Dormouse numbers may be recovering in England and Wales after years of decline, offering a rare piece of good news for one of our best-loved mammals. The writer and podcaster on why politics is made to seem more complicated than it is and his mission to unpack world events for everyone Why did you get into comedy? My mum was a professional dancer and always encouraged me to perform. Given that I have zero rhythm, comedy was my other option. She wrote me a poem called Mrs Brown’s Moggy, about a cat that was often very soggy, for my school’s talent show. Because you can’t tell the difference between real and polite laughter at the age of six, I assumed I’d killed my first gig and convinced myself I was born to do nothing else.

Larson finished fourth in the opening stage to secure his third Cup title and become NASCAR’s first back-to-back champion since Jimmie Johnson in 2010 Tyler Reddick won the opening stage, while Kyle Larson placed fourth, scoring seven stage points. Here's everything to know about the DLS method and all the ways by which scores are calculated under the rain check. DLS calculates targets using resources, meaning overs remaining and wickets in hand together. The VJD method is the only serious modern rival, and it is used in Indian domestic cricket. Earlier systems failed because they ignored wickets, most notoriously at the 1992 World Cup. The Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method is the system cricket uses to reset a target when rain or any other interruption shortens a limited-overs match. It was devised by two English statisticians, Frank Duckworth and Tony Lewis, introduced in 1997 and adopted by the ICC two years later.

When a user chooses the “Yes, and don’t ask again” option to approve running a command, that choice gets stored as part of a rule in the local “.claude/settings.local.json” file on the user’s computer. That rule is sometimes coded as a pattern, but the command itself is often written to that settings file as is, including any sensitive information that may be embedded within it.

A surprising discovery suggests that some early signs of Alzheimer’s disease may begin outside the brain. Using miniature laboratory systems made from human cells, scientists found that genetic mutations associated with inherited Alzheimer’s can disrupt nerve-to-muscle connections without any involvement from the brain or spinal cord. This could help explain why some patients experience changes in balance, walking, and coordination long before memory problems develop. Alzheimer's disease is best known for its effects on memory and thinking, but new research suggests that some symptoms may develop in a surprising place: outside the brain.

Goaltender Pekka Rinne, the Nashville Predators' all-time leader in wins, was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Nov. 9. Pekka Rinne was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Nov. 9, joining the Class of 2026 that includes Patrice Bergeron, Carey Price, Cindy Curley, Keith Tkachuk and Brian Burke. "I'm humbled to be standing here amongst all my heroes," Rinne said from the stage at Brookfield Place in Toronto. "I'd be lying if I said I saw this coming." Rinne is the Predators' all-time leader in wins (369), shutouts (60), saves (17,627) and playoff wins (45). He won the Vezina Trophy as the league's top goaltender in 2018 and the King Clancy Memorial Trophy in 2021.

The remains will be taken to Nagaland, where tribal leaders plan a joint memorial and burial. The University of Oxford has returned the remains of 39 people taken from the Naga community during British colonial rule in India. There are plans to bury them under a joint memorial in a park in Nagaland.
